description: Scanned filter: a vibrating mass-spring string sets the gains of sixteen bandpass filters, so the physics plays the equaliser and the spectrum ripples and decays on its own

params.text: Sets how hard the springs pull one mass towards the next, which is how fast a ripple travels along the string
Sets how fast the string's motion dies: quick at the top of its travel, ringing long and slightly self-oscillating at the very bottom
Sets how often the string physics are stepped, 500Hz at the bottom of its travel to 8000Hz at the top, which is how fast the spectrum evolves
Morphs the hammer profile a hit imposes on the string, from a sine through a sawtooth and noise to a pair of pulses
Drives the string continuously with the hammer profile, so the filterbank keeps moving without any triggers
Sets the resonance of the sixteen bandpass filters, a Q of 2 at the bottom of its travel to 40 at the top; high settings turn a pluck into a ringing chime
Sets the lowest of the sixteen bands, 40Hz at the bottom of its travel to 2000Hz at the top
Sets how many octaves the sixteen bands cover above the lowest, one at the bottom of its travel to six at the top
Crossfades between the signal coming in and the filtered one, 0% dry and 100% filtered
Hammers every mass to the hammer profile, a pluck

inputs.text: Added to the damp knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the rate knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the base knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the spread knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
A rising edge through 1V hammers every mass to the hammer profile, a pluck
The signal the sixteen bandpass filters work on

outputs.text: The filtered signal crossfaded against the dry one by the mix knob, ±5V

notes: at rest the string is flat and the filtered signal is silent. With force at the bottom nothing comes out of the wet path until the string is hit.
the string's displacement is bipolar, so a band can invert the phase of its slice, which adds hollow comb-like movement on wideband material.
the string engine is scando's, and the same controls behave the same way here.
